Hi Laura — thanks for the clear ask and for the PO. Short answer: we can support both workflows, but the recommended approach depends on VAT jurisdiction and how your AP wants to remit. High level options: 

1) Separate invoices (one invoice per Acero legal entity). Pros: clean VAT/reclaim trail per company in EU; cons: requires each entity to be set up as a billing account in our system.

2) Single invoice with split lines and entity/tax-id fields. Pros: one invoice for your AP to pay; cons: may require extra fields for VAT reclaim and we need confirmation if your AP will remit multiple wires or one combined payment.

I've attached a CSV template "acero_invoice_split_template.csv" and our generic "redwood-remit-instructions.pdf" showing bank/ACH details and our preferred remittance references. Can you fill the template with: entity legal name, tax ID, billing email, cost center, PO line, and amount per line?

Looping in Kimberly from accounting for the final tax/bank guidance and Grace on ops for any billing-account setup work.

Next steps: once we have the populated CSV + confirmation of whether AP will send separate wires, accounting will advise whether separate invoices are required.

Best,

Hi Laura / Rishi,

Accounting notes / requirements: 

- If two of Acero's entities are EU VAT-registered and you want each entity to reclaim VAT independently, our preference is to issue separate invoices per legal entity. That ensures a straightforward VAT invoice with the correct supplier VAT ID and tax breakdown.

- If you prefer a single invoice, it must include explicit per-line tax IDs and the VAT amount per entity; please confirm whether Acero will perform an internal allocation after payment or if you expect Redwood to net-settle.

Required fields in the CSV template (mandatory): entity_legal_name, entity_tax_id (formatted with country code), billing_email, cost_center_code, PO_number, PO_line_description, amount_ex_vat, vat_rate, total_amount. Missing tax IDs will force us to default to our standard supplier VAT and may prevent reclaim.

We will also need bank-account proof for any wire to be accepted from an EU entity (anti-fraud). I'm attaching a short bank proof sample: "redwood-bank-proof.pdf". For split wires (multiple beneficiary banks), we can accept up to three separate wires against the same PO — please state the remittance amounts in the CSV.

Two quick asks for Acero: 1) include the target invoice date (e.g., 2026-12-01) in the CSV; 2) confirm which legal entity should receive the subscription license (if you need seat assignment per entity that needs to be reflected in the contract).

If you'd like, we can put the billing terms (separate invoices) into a brief amendment and route via DocuSign — that speeds up legal/PO matching.

Regards,
